text: The addition of dilute NaOH to $Cr^{3+}$ salt solution will give :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Hydroxide ions added in small amount to a $\mathrm{Cr}{}^{3+}$ solution give a green gelatinous precipitate. This solid contains no discrete $\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{OH}){}_{3}$ molecules; it is hydrated chromium(III) oxide, $\mathrm{Cr}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{n}$, of variable water content, and $\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{OH}){}_{3}$ is only an idealised way of writing it.

The precipitate is amphoteric and redissolves only in excess alkali as the soluble chromite ion $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{OH}){}_{4}]^{-}$ or $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{OH}){}_{6}]^{3-}$, so dilute $\mathrm{NaOH}$ gives neither a solution of $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{OH}){}_{4}]^{-}$ nor a precipitate of the soluble anion $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{OH}){}_{6}]^{3-}$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : Ethyl pent-4-yn-oate on reaction with $CH_{3}$MgBr gives a 3${}^{\circ }$-alcohol.

Statement II : In this reaction one mole of ethyl pent-4-yn-oate utilizes two moles of $CH_{3}$MgBr.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Ethyl pent-4-ynoate is $\mathrm{HC}\equiv \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{COOC}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}$.

The terminal $\equiv \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}$ is acidic, so the first mole of $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$ acts as a base and removes it, releasing methane:

$\mathrm{HC}\equiv \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COOC}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}+\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}\longrightarrow \mathrm{BrMgC}\equiv \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COOC}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}+\mathrm{CH}{}_{4}$

The ester group then takes two more moles: the first adds to $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}$ and expels $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{O}{}^{-}$ to give a methyl ketone, and the second adds to this ketone to give a tertiary alkoxide.


[IMG]

Hydrolysis gives $\mathrm{HC}\equiv \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$ (2-methylhex-5-yn-2-ol), a $3^{\circ }$ alcohol, so Statement I is true.

One mole of the ester uses $1+2=3$ moles of $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$, not two, so Statement II is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift

text: Which one of the following reactions will not yield propionic acid?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}$ is a methyl ketone, so hypoiodite gives the iodoform reaction, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}+3\mathrm{OI}{}^{-}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COO}{}^{-}+\mathrm{CHI}{}_{3}+2\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}$, and acidification gives $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COOH}$, propionic acid.

(B) Propane, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, has no functional group or benzylic hydrogen and is not oxidised by alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO}{}_{4}$, so no propionic acid is formed.

(C) Alkaline hydrolysis of the $\mathrm{CCl}{}_{3}$ group gives $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH}){}_{3}$, which loses water to give $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COO}{}^{-}$; acidification gives propionic acid.

(D) $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{Br}$ forms $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{MgBr}$, which adds to $\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}$; hydrolysis then gives $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COOH}$, butanoic acid, one carbon longer than propionic acid.

Hence, the correct options are (B) and (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift

text:
Which one of the following is the major product of the given reaction?


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Two equivalents of $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$ react with both electrophilic groups: one adds to the $\mathrm{C}\equiv \mathrm{N}$ group to give an imine magnesium salt, and the other adds to the ring C=O to give a magnesium alkoxide.

$\mathrm{H}{}_{3}\mathrm{O}{}^{+}$ hydrolyses the imine salt to a methyl ketone, so $-\mathrm{CN}$ becomes $-\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}$, and converts the alkoxide to a tertiary alcohol: C-2 now carries $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ and OH, between C-1 (benzylic, $\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$) and C-3 ($\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$).

Hot $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$ dehydrates the tertiary alcohol through the tertiary carbocation at C-2. Loss of the benzylic H from C-1 gives a C-1=C-2 double bond that is tetrasubstituted and conjugated with the benzene ring, the most stable alkene.

Loss of H from C-3 would give a C=C not conjugated with the ring (option D), and options B and C wrongly keep the $-\mathrm{CN}$ group.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift

text:
The major product (A) formed in the reaction given below is :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The substrate $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5})\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{Br}$ is a primary bromide whose only $β$-carbon is branched and carries a benzylic hydrogen.

$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{O}{}^{-}$ is a strong base; the benzylic $β$-H is relatively acidic and its removal gives a double bond conjugated with the benzene ring, while backside attack at the $β$-branched $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{Br}$ carbon is hindered, so E2 dominates over $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$.

$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5})\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{Br}+\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{O}{}^{-}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5})=\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}+\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{OH}+\mathrm{Br}{}^{-}$

The major product A is 2-phenylbut-1-ene; the methyl ether is only the minor substitution product.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: The number of optical isomers possible for [$Cr(C_{2}O_{4})_{3}$]$^{3-}$ is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{4}){}_{3}]{}^{3-}$ is an octahedral complex of the type $[\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{AA}){}_{3}]$, in which each oxalate ion spans two cis positions.

With three identical chelate rings there is only one geometrical arrangement, but it has no plane or centre of symmetry, so its mirror image cannot be superimposed on it.


[IMG]

The complex therefore exists as one pair of enantiomers, the $\Delta$ and $\Lambda$ forms.

Hence, the answer is 2.

text:
Two flasks I and II shown below are connected by a valve of negligible volume.


[IMG]

When the valve is opened, the final pressure of the system in bar is x $\times$ $10^{-2}$. The value of x is $__________. ($Integer answer)

[Assume - Ideal gas; 1 bar $= 10^{5} Pa$; Molar mass of $N_{2} = 28.0 g$ mol$^{-1}$; R = 8.31 J mol$^{-1} K^{-1}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Applying; $(n_{I} + n_{II})_{$initial$} = (n_{I} + n_{II})_{$final}

$\Rightarrow$ Assuming the system attains a final temperature of T (such that 60 < T < 300)

$\Rightarrow$ $⎛⎝⎜\begin{array}{l} Heatlostby \\ N_{2}ofcontainer \\ I \end{array}⎞⎠⎟=⎛⎝⎜\begin{array}{l} Heatgainedby \\ N_{2}ofcontainer \\ II \end{array}⎞⎠⎟$

$\Rightarrow$ $n_{1}C_{m}(300$ $-$ $T) = n_{II}C_{m}(T$ $-$ 60)

$\Rightarrow \left (\frac{2.8}{28}\right )(300-T)=\frac{0.2}{28}(T-60)$

$\Rightarrow$ 14(300 $-$ T) = T $-$ 60

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{(14\times 300+60)}{15}=T$

$\Rightarrow$ T = 284 K (final temperature)

$\Rightarrow$ If the final pressure = P

$\Rightarrow$ $(n_{I} + n_{II})_{$final} = $\left (\frac{3.0}{28}\right )$

$\Rightarrow\frac{P}{RT}(V_{I}+V_{II})=\frac{3.0gm}{28gm/mol}$

$P=\left (\frac{3}{28}mol\right )\times 8.31\frac{J}{mol-K}\times \frac{284K}{3\times 10^{-3}m^{3}}\times 10^{-5}\frac{bar}{Pa}$

$\Rightarrow$ 0.84287 bar

$\Rightarrow$ 84.28 $\times$ $10^{-2}$ bar

$\Rightarrow$ 84

text:
The number of photons emitted by a monochromatic (single frequency) infrared range finder of power 1 mW and wavelength of 1000 nm, in 0.1 second is x $\times$ $10^{13}$. The value of x is $_____________. ($Nearest integer)

= 0.1 sec. $\times$ $10^{-3}\frac{J}{s}$

$\Rightarrow$ 50 (nearest integer)

solution.body:
$T_{\min }=\left (\frac{\Delta ^{0}H}{\Delta ^{0}S}\right )$

$\left [\Delta ^{0}S(FeO)+\Delta ^{0}S(C_{(graphite)})\right ]$

$=[27.28+197.6]-[57.49+5.74]$

= 161.65 J/mol-K

$T_{\min }=\frac{155.8\times 10^{3}J/mol}{161.65J/mol-K}=963.8$ K

$\simeq 964$ k (nearest integer)
